# The 2026 overbuild (generated by tools/overbuild_2026.py)

Completion lag 17 months: building in 2026, 2027 = 0.945 x consents lagged 17 months (all categories; consents observed to 2026-07-01).
2026: consents 33,879 -> building 32,016; requirement 19,313 -> excess +12,702.
2027: consents 40,908 -> building 38,658; requirement 26,207 -> excess +12,451.
gap_ref = building 2027 - requirement 2028 (26,810) = +11,848, fading from 2028 at rho = 0.434.
Booked as surplus: market excess +34,229, absorbed -34,229, net -0 dwellings over 2026-2050 (variant REF; absorbed by 2035).
Implied vacancy (1 - households / (stock + surplus still vacant)): peak 6.63% in 2028, 5.39% in 2050 (the vacancy-rate parameter: its published 2023 census value, 5.39%); census 1986-2023 range 5.08-8.09% (empty dwellings; before 2013 the empty share of unoccupied is estimated, and 2013->2018 is a definitional break).
Consistent definition (pooled 2018/2023 empty share of unoccupied, 49.2%): 1986 4.42%, 1991 4.64%, 1996 4.01%, 2001 4.81%, 2006 4.80%, 2013 5.22%, 2018 5.08%, 2023 5.38%.
Sensitivity, booked as redevelopment: implied net removals peak at 16,194 in 2026 (default: 3,492).

Limitation: The vacancy-rate parameter is held at its published 2023 census value (5.39%; on the consistent definition 2023 is the series maximum, 5.38%, minimum 4.01% in 1996); the 2026 overbuild raises implied stock vacancy temporarily and is absorbed by 2035, so implied vacancy returns to the parameter (5.39% in 2050). The 2026 overbuild (market excess ≈34,200 dwellings over 2026-2050, of which ≈30,300 in 2026-2028) is absorbed by 2035 along the normalised logistic of the levers (≈34,200 dwellings built less; implied vacancy peaks at 6.63% in 2028). Stock-flow theory of the housing market (Rosen & Smith 1983; Wheaton 1990; DiPasquale & Wheaton 1992; Gabriel & Nothaft 2001) fixes the direction, reversion of vacancy to its equilibrium rate, not the speed; 2035 is the common RECC adoption window of the model and the speed is bracketed by sensitivity rows (never absorbed, by 2030, by 2045). The persistence rho = 0.43 describes how the flow deviation fades, not the payback of the stock.
